title: KS-695 F5: build the dedicated `subjects:erase` scope gate on POST /api/gdpr/erasures — Kam ruled it 2026-09-03 and it has never been built
description:
**Category 1. Medium. AUTHORISED, UNFILED — creation refused by Linear's free-tier cap.**

## BLUF

**Kam ruled this on 2026-09-03 09:56 (Wednesday's card** `secuura-erasure-scope-gate`**, option A) and it has never been built.** `POST /api/gdpr/erasures` — the connector erasure route Platform S calls — has **no scope gate at all**, while `/api/anchoring` requires `anchors:write`. Connector JWTs already carry scopes, so the machinery exists and this route simply does not use it.

**Kam's ruling, verbatim:** *"Dedicated scope* `subjects:erase` *— mint it for S's key at registration; refuse others 403."*

## Delivery status — measured, not recalled

`git grep subjects:erase` over `develop` at `52f676d9b` returns **0 hits**. Control: `git grep documents:read` returns **3**, including `api-gateway/src/middleware/scopes.ts`, so the search reaches the scope machinery and the null is a real absence rather than a search that could not match.

## Why it was not built when it was found

The session that found it (Peter's #790 F5) recommended a dedicated scope and **deliberately did not implement it**, on the grounds that widening or narrowing an authorisation check is not an agent's call. Kam's ruling is that call. It has been outstanding since 2026-09-03.

## Scope of the work

1. **Registry entry** for `subjects:erase` alongside the existing scopes.
2. **Mint it for Platform S's connector key at registration** — this is why the ticket belongs to the **S↔K stream**: S's `sk_` key is re-minted, so the change is not K-internal.
3. **Refuse callers without it with 403** on `POST /api/gdpr/erasures` (and the status read, if the same gate applies — decide and state which).
4. **Red-proof on the wire**: a key without the scope must be refused by name, with a positive control proving a key carrying it succeeds, and a second control separating the scope refusal from an ordinary auth failure.

## Cross-references

* Ruled on KS-695 as its own numbered item (s137, 2026-09-06), explicitly **distinct from ask 3** — see KS-695 comment `e985996d`, which un-conflated the two after the phrase had already been carried into a session brief and would otherwise have been built as the wrong thing.
* Ask 3 is the connector-scoped organisation erasure, shape (a), ruled 2026-09-02. Different ruling, different work.

## Provenance

Wednesday's ruling mail 2026-09-05T22:20:55Z (SPF + DKIM `header.i=@agentmail.to` + DMARC pass), reading the card store `decisions.json` directly. Creation attempted and refused by `USAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED / activeIssueCount`; **nothing archived to make room** (Kam's `secuura-linear-cap-2` ruling is HOLD).

---

*Filed by s138 (seat A) 2026-09-06. Text authored by s137 and preserved at* `5_Project_History/unfiled-tickets-s137/unfiled-erasure-scope-ticket.md`*; creation was refused by Linear's cap on 2026-09-05T23:33:40Z and retried after Kam upgraded the plan (panel, 09:45).*

**BLUF:** Kam ruled this question on 2026-11-05 16:10:04 AEDT (card `secuura-ks843-erasure-flip-trigger-1105`): option **a**, "Keep logged grace; flip after 30 days of zero un-scoped Platform S erasure calls".

Question as asked: "KS-843: what evidence flips SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED, given you ruled no re-mint?"

The build is queued to a lane seat. This ticket stays In Progress.
No re-mint (KS-889 ruled b): the flip waits for other evidence; logged grace continues.

## BLUF
@stuart.jamieson we want to tighten the erasure endpoint this week, and for that we need two answers from you: **a window this week when Platform S can switch to new keys, and roughly how long that switch takes on your side.** Nothing changes for Platform S until we have agreed the window with you.

## What we need from you
1. A window this week (day and time, with your timezone) when you can switch Platform S to the new keys.
2. Your best estimate of how long the switch takes, from the moment you receive a new key to the moment Platform S is using it everywhere. A rough figure is fine ("about 30 minutes", "about a day"). We will keep the old keys working for longer than your estimate, so Platform S is never cut off part-way.

## Why
Today the erasure endpoint (the request and the status read) accepts any Platform S key. We have built the stricter rule, that only a key carrying an explicit erasure permission is accepted, and it is running in a "log it, but allow it" mode. To turn the stricter rule on, Platform S's keys have to be replaced by new ones that carry that permission. We have decided to start now.

## What happens if we do nothing
Nothing breaks for Platform S. But the endpoint keeps accepting any Platform S key, the stricter rule stays off, and this ticket stays open past 31 October.

## How it would go, so you can plan
1. You tell us the window and the switch time.
2. We create the new keys and keep the old ones working for longer than your estimate. We agree with you how the new keys reach you. After that overlap the old keys stop working, so the switch has to happen inside it.
3. You switch Platform S over, inside the window.
4. We watch our logs until they show Platform S calling with the new keys, then turn the stricter rule on and tell you.

We will not replace any key or switch anything on before you have confirmed the window.

Posted by the Platform K agent on Kam's behalf.

## BLUF
**Built and merged; the enforcing half waits on a Kam step. Leaves the lot as a card for Kam.** I touched nothing about the Platform S keys or the flag.

## Recommendation
Kam's call, as already ruled on 2026-09-06 (option A, logged grace): pick the cutover window with Stuart, rotate Platform S's connector keys with `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS` set for that window (the 09-08 note on this ticket explains why, to avoid a 401 on every S call), then flip `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED` once the log shows S on the new key. Until then the ticket's item 3 (refuse callers without the scope) holds only in grace mode.

## Detail
- **Built, on develop:** the scope and its mint (PR #841), the gate on both erasure routes with the F-7 and F-9 rounds (merge `ba28db317`), and the canonical-path fix (#1019, squash `581c9db0d`). The `ks843-erasure-scope-gate` and `ks843-erasure-path-bypass` cells run in the 876-test green suite.
- **Live on Kintsugi:** `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED` is unset (grace) and the gateway log holds 0 `[KS-843]` lines since the 10-07 deploy, so Platform S has not used the door there. A human OWNER token is refused `403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` at the door.
- **Why not Done:** deployed code that does not yet enforce is not the end state the ruling describes.

Verified 2026-10-12 by Seat K 4th (lane K, verify-and-close lot L02) in a clean clone of develop `65d7722f83a6`. Kintsugi (`secuura02-kintsugi-vm`) runs revision `69f2045af2a4f5f0b83b2f76c62514512abdc7b5`, deployed 2026-10-07; the gateway container was created 2026-10-07T04:48:05Z and has 0 restarts. Kintsugi runs `NODE_ENV=development`. Gateway suite on develop: 97 files / 876 tests, 0 failed. Evidence: project history folder `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatK-4th/` (`box/`, `redproof/`, `live/`, `tickets/`).

## Your cutover ruling still holds — but with #880 merged it needs one parameter it used to get for free

**BLUF: Kam's 2026-09-06 ruling (option A, logged grace) is PRESERVED, not changed.** Nothing here re-opens it. What changes is that one step of it — rotating Platform S's connector keys — stops being safe *by default* the moment [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) / [#880](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/880) merges, and needs an explicit setting instead.

Raised here because the dependency was findable from this ticket but not from #880, which is how it nearly reached a merge unexamined.

### What the ruling says, verbatim

> **Kam ruled 2026-09-06 13:59 (card `secuura-ks843-cutover-stuart`, option A): logged grace.** … **Platform S's connector keys are rotated, and the switch flips to scope-only once the log shows S on the new key.** Not before.

Option A was chosen for a stated reason: *"Never breaks S; no synchronised window with Stuart needed."*

### Why #880 removes that property, measured from the code

`revokePriorConnectorKeys` (`services/security/src/index.ts`) reads `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS`, **defaulting to `'0'`**:

* `grace = 0` → `UPDATE svc_api_keys SET is_active = false WHERE connector_id = $1 AND tenant_id = $2::uuid AND id <> $3 AND is_active = true` — **immediate**.
* `grace > 0` → `expires_at = LEAST(COALESCE(expires_at,'infinity'), NOW() + grace)` — a bounded overlap.

It runs only `if (data.rotate && data.connectorId)`, and the gateway passes `connectorId: platform-s:${externalRef}` — so it lands **exactly on S's prior keys for that externalRef**, in that tenant, and nothing else.

**Two consequences worth stating precisely:**

1. **It is a 401, not a 403.** Revocation kills the key at *authentication*, above `requireScopeOrRole` — so it breaks **every endpoint S calls**, not only the erasure path this cutover concerns.
2. **The ruling's trigger condition stops being observable.** Option A flips to scope-only *"once the log shows S on the new key"*. At `grace = 0` there is no interval in which S is transitioning — the old key works, then it 401s. The `[KS-843]` log evidence the flip depends on cannot accrue.

**This ticket already predicted it.** From its own Related section: *"KS-577 — … for this cutover it happens to provide the overlap window that makes a zero-downtime swap possible. Named so nobody mistakes the convenience for a reason to leave it open."* That paragraph was right. What was missing was anything connecting it to #880's merge decision.

### The remedy — no code change, and Kam's default stays as he ruled

Either of these preserves option A exactly:

* **Set `API_KEY_ROTATION_GRACE_SECONDS`** to the agreed cutover window on the security service for the rotation, then unset it. #880 already implements this path.
* **Or mint with `rotate: false`** for the cutover — purely additive, i.e. today's behaviour — and perform the real `rotate: true` retirement once the log shows S migrated.

**#880's default of `0` is not being challenged**: it is what Kam ruled on 2026-08-07 and the docblock says so. The cutover sets the parameter for its own window; the default stands.

### Not done here

Not raised with Stuart — the cutover conversation is Kam's to open. #880 untouched. This is a record of a precondition, not a proposal to change either ruling.

*Reciprocal note on KS-577 / #880 so the dependency is findable from both ends.*

## Measured on the demo box — a backfill is NOT possible; re-mint is the only path

**BLUF: NO.** Nothing on the `svc_api_keys` row determines the connector for the pre-existing keys. A backfill would recover **5 of 32 active keys (16%)**, leave 26 with no evidence at all, and one is ambiguous. That is not a backfill, it is a partial guess — so the only sound path is a **re-mint of Platform S's keys**.

### The window, measured (read-only, on the demo VM)

| Reading | Value |
|---|---|
| `svc_api_keys` rows | **39** before the probe (the brief said 43 — the measured number is 39) |
| rows with `connector_id` | **0** |
| still active with a null connector | **32** |

### Can anything imply the connector?

The only other connector reference on K is `action_provenance.connector_id` — 4680 rows, all populated, **6 distinct connectors**, carrying `organization_id`. That is the only candidate join. Against the null-connector keys:

| Connectors implied by the key's org | Keys | Active keys |
|---|---|---|
| **0 — no evidence at all** | 33 | **26** |
| 1 — unambiguous | 5 | 5 |
| 2 — ambiguous | 1 | 1 |

`action_provenance` covers **6 organisations**; the null-connector keys span **21 distinct organisations, and 18 of them carry no `organization_id` at all**. So for the large majority there is simply nothing on K to join to.

**Control:** the same join returns non-zero for organisations known to have provenance (e.g. `bb9d5300…` → 1, `aeb2e3b1…` → 2), so a 0 means "no evidence", not "the query cannot match". The first run of this query failed on a `uuid = text` mismatch and was re-run with an explicit cast — the numbers above are from the corrected query.

### What follows

The KS-843 cutover flip's prerequisite cannot be met by a migration. **The re-mint is Stuart's window and Kam's call** — this comment records the measurement; it is not a request to anyone, and no message has gone to Platform S from here.

*s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, on the demo box after the leg-2 rebuild (`security` current, `connector_id` live).*

## ⚠ Correction — KS-869 merging is NOT sufficient for the cutover flip

My earlier comment here (`6b975c92…`) said the flip's prerequisite is **KS-869 merged**. **That is not enough, and I am correcting it before anyone acts on it.**

KS-869 merged today (`50913d2c3`). But its `COALESCE` backfill has an **empty window** for keys that already exist: `memApiKeys` warms only from the database at boot, so every pre-fix row re-warms with `connectorId` undefined, every later save passes NULL, and COALESCE correctly declines it. **Backfill happens only for keys minted after KS-869 deploys.**

**So the `[KS-843]` grace log will still record `connectorId: null` for every EXISTING Platform S key.** Kam's 13:59 ruling flips the switch *"once the log shows S on the new key"* — and the log still cannot say which connector it is looking at.

**The real prerequisite is KS-889**, which carries the measurement that decides it: does anything on the row (`key_prefix`, `organization_id`, `name`) determine the connector? If yes, a one-off backfill. If no, **Platform S's keys must be re-minted** — Stuart's window, therefore Kam's call, and it belongs with the KS-577 rotation conversation rather than as a separate ask.

**Also note:** `security` was not in today's demo rebuild set (its `src` did not change), so the box still runs Sept-3 security code. KS-869's behaviour is on `develop`, not yet on the demo.

The erasure door itself **is** live on the demo as of `14914258c`, in **grace** mode — the ruled shape. Nothing has changed for Platform S.

## The demo hold is LIFTED — Kam, 2026-09-06 15:12 AEST

His words, verbatim: *"the items tested not deployed. lets deploy and archive these"* (15:06), and asked directly whether that lifts the demo stop — *"yes. lift until we get through these tickets and the backlog."* (15:12)

**Scope in his own framing: a window, until the Tested-Not-Deployed set and the backlog are worked through.** The demo box only; production is untouched (there is none in scope).

**This ticket's deploy is therefore unblocked**, subject to the plan below.

## ⚠ The recorded hold ticket cannot carry this note

The hold has been referred to all day as **KS-641**. That ticket was **archived 2026-09-05T06:45:19Z** and Linear refuses comments on it (`commentCreate` → *"Entity not found: Issue"*, while the same id reads fine — the archived-issue signature). So the lift is recorded here and on the sibling ticket instead of there. The hold was always Kam's word carried in the briefs; KS-641 was only ever its label.

## ⚠ And the deploy path in the commission is the wrong one

The commission named `deployment/azure/deploy.sh` and `.github/workflows/deploy-demo.yml`. **Neither is the live demo.** Both target the Container Apps estate **deleted 2026-07-31** — `deploy-demo.yml`'s own guard input reads *"this path deploys the DELETED Container Apps estate, NOT the live VM demo."*

The live demo is a **single VM** (`secuura02-demo-vm`, `20.212.118.59`), stack at `/home/secuura/secuura/Dev`, redeployed by rsync + `docker compose build` + `up -d`. Verified reachable read-only just now: aarch64, 32 containers up, **disk 80% full (13 GiB free)**, **1.7 GiB RAM available**. Those two numbers are the real constraint on an on-box ARM64 rebuild, not the deploy command.

Nothing is built or shipped until that plan is confirmed.

**For this ticket specifically:** the erasure door deploys in **grace mode**, which is exactly the shape Kam's 13:59 logged-grace ruling calls for — nothing changes for Platform S. The **flip** to scope-only remains blocked on **KS-869** (PR #854), because until `connector_id` is persisted the grace log records `connectorId: null` after a restart and cannot say which connector was admitted.

## BLUF — the cutover flip now has a prerequisite: KS-869

**The `[KS-843]` grace log's `connectorId` is NULL for every Platform S key after a security-service restart.** `svc_api_keys.connector_id` exists as a column and is **never written and never read** (KS-869) — the association lives in the in-process map only.

**Until KS-869 ships, the log cannot say WHICH connector was admitted.** So Kam's 2026-09-06 13:59 ruling — *flip to scope-only once the log shows S on the new key* — has a prerequisite: **KS-869 merged, and the log observed after a restart.**

**Kam's ruling stands unchanged.** Logged grace is still the shape; what gains a prerequisite is the *mechanism that produces the evidence for the flip*, not the decision.

**Nothing changes for Platform S. Nothing deploys (KS-641).**

## The chain, traced end to end

```
security  /api/keys/validate :1182  →  connectorId: apiKey.connectorId || null
gateway   auth.ts:230               →  meta.connectorId = data.connectorId || ''
gateway   auth.ts:272               →  userId = `connector:${meta.connectorId || 'api-key'}`
gateway   auth.ts:281               →  req.user.connectorId = meta.connectorId
scopes.ts (the grace log)           →  connectorId: user.connectorId ?? null
```

After a restart every connector also collapses to `userId = connector:api-key`, so audit attribution loses the same distinction.

KS-869 is in build now, with a **driven** restart as its red-proof rather than the static read that found it.

## BLUF — MERGED. Three rounds, two holes, both closed.

**#845 merged as `ba28db317f982045567ecab13ae4956925bb3a2f`** (tree `8457a3a776e1f492600527b175d3e84c6cbd77c9`, first parent `af0782572` = the asserted tip, 7 files +821 −5). The **third tier-1 gate PASSED** (2026-09-06T04:43:36Z). **Nothing deployed — the demo hold stands (KS-641).**

## The door's behaviour, as the tester measured it

| principal / mode | result |
|---|---|
| unauthenticated | **401** |
| `connector` role, no scope, **enforcing** | **403**, upstream never called |
| `connector` role, no scope, **grace** (default) | **200**, 1 upstream hit, **1 `[KS-843]` warn** |
| holder of `subjects:erase`, either mode | **200**, 1 upstream hit |

Driven across **14 gated spellings × 5 principals — 530 rows** — plus a replica of originate's own mount.

## The three rounds

| round | verdict | report |
|---|---|---|
| pass 1 @ `87450b54c` | findings F-1…F-8 | `…-s138-ks843-845-half2-87450b54c/` |
| re-gate @ `59248bf38` | **NO GO** — F-9 regression, F-10 undisclosed coverage loss | `…-s138-ks843-845-half2-regate-59248bf38/` |
| round 3 @ `e1d9d9380` | **PASS** | `…-round3-e1d9d9380/` |

**F-9** — round 2 replaced express's matching with a case-sensitive regex, so six case spellings (`ERASURES`, `Erasures`, `Erasures/`, `//ERASURES`, `/API/GDPR/ERASURES`, `GET …/ERASURES/abc`) ran originate's erasure handler in enforcing mode for a principal with neither scope nor role. Round 3 gave the matching back to express (an inner `Router` mounted at `/erasures`, fed the separator-collapsed `req.url`): **all six now 403 / 0 hits**, and the erasure handler ran **0 times** at the replica where round 2 ran it on all six. **F-7 stayed closed** — six separator shapes and both exact paths. The 20-shape evasion table was re-derived and **nothing newly opened**.

**F-10** — the restored `S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES` mint-set cell **diffs EMPTY** against the parent's copy (26 lines).

## Residues — filed per defect, none of them blockers

- **KS-870** (P3) — F-11: every *admitted* erasure authenticates twice (refused 1 / admitted 2), doubling a remote key validation on a partner path.
- **KS-871** (P3) — F-12: the audit log reads `req.path` *after* the response, so a **refused** erasure is logged as `/`. Began at round 2, went one level further at round 3. **Whether it is latent or live is UNMEASURED** — the tester did not run the middleware and could not tell if `isDbAvailable()` is ever true on the demo.
- **KS-872** (P3) — O-3: `packages/shared` project `tsc` is red on develop (`crypto.JsonWebKey` gone in `@types/node` 26.1.0). **Not this commit** — the diff against `packages/shared` is empty.

## Residues recorded here rather than filed

- **O-1** — the six *separator* spellings' "logged exactly once" is asserted by no cell. The **case** grace cell asserts the log; the separator grace cell asserts 200 + 1 hit only. One line (a warn spy + count) closes it on the next touch of that file.
- **O-2** — the `req.url` restore has **source-pin coverage only**. The proxy collapses separators on the way out, so no upstream-facing assertion can see the difference. A declared limit, not an oversight.
- **O-4** — the comment strip in the F-7+F-9 source cell is **conservative**: it fails safe on a trailing comment. **Do not "fix" it into a fail-open strip.**

## ⚠ Read this alongside KS-869 before acting on the cutover

Kam's logged-grace ruling (comment `fc148e79…`) makes the flip conditional on *"the log shows S on the new key"*. **KS-869 — filed today — is that `connectorId` is never persisted**, so after a security-service restart the `[KS-843]` warn records `connectorId: null` and cannot say which connector was admitted. **The cutover evidence is weaker than this ticket previously described.** KS-869 should land before anyone reads that log as a basis for flipping `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED`.

## BLUF — Kam ruled the cutover: LOGGED GRACE

**Kam ruled 2026-09-06 13:59 (card `secuura-ks843-cutover-stuart`, option A): logged grace.** The gate ships as **role-OR-scope with a refusal log and a scope-only switch** — which is already the shape built on this ticket. **Platform S's connector keys are rotated, and the switch flips to scope-only once the log shows S on the new key.** Not before.

**Nothing deploys under the demo hold (KS-641).** This ruling sets the *shape*, not a release.

## What that means in the code as it stands

`requireScopeOrRole(subjects:erase, ['connector'], SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED)`:

- **Switch unset (today's default):** a `connector`-role key without the scope is **admitted and logged** — one `[KS-843]` line per request carrying the connector id, org, tenant, method, the URL as the caller typed it, and the granted scopes. That log is the cutover evidence.
- **Switch `'true'`:** the same caller is **refused 403**. A holder of `subjects:erase` passes in both modes.
- The flag is read per request and anything unset, empty or misspelled leaves the grace **on** — a typo must never silently start refusing a partner.

## Why the flip cannot happen yet, precisely

K has no way to add a scope to an existing key: the security service exposes create / list / revoke / validate — no PATCH, and no `UPDATE svc_api_keys` anywhere in it. So every connector key minted before the scope existed lacks it permanently. The rotation is the only path, and the log is the only proof it has happened.

## The Stuart ask — coming from Kam, not from here

Two things are needed before the switch can be flipped, and they come to Stuart **from Kam as a test block**, not from this ticket: how many connector keys Platform S holds against the K demo, and a rotation window. Recorded here so the dependency is visible on the ticket rather than living in a thread.

## Round 3 status

Round 2's re-gate was a NO GO on **F-9**, a case-sensitivity regression it introduced. Kam authorised one narrow round 3 (card `secuura-ks843-half2-round3`, option A); it is pushed at **`e1d9d93803780f50152ab2d7d31e6e30007d37af`** on PR #845 and awaiting its third tier-1 gate. Residue and acceptance rows are on **KS-861**.

## BLUF

**The #845 re-gate came back NO GO at round 2 of 2 (2026-09-06T02:45:01Z, tier 1, head `59248bf3841ac0354f1c2ae0e8600756d26d828d`). The cap is spent. #845 is HELD and unmerged — nothing ships on it, and there are no commits on `kamilkreiser/ks-843-half2-erasure-gate-r2`.**

## Recommendation

**Hold.** The entire residue is filed as **one ticket, KS-861** (Backlog, P2, linked here and to KS-858). A round 3 starts **only** on Kam's ruling on the card `secuura-ks843-half2-round3` (recommendation A = one narrow round 3; default B = hold), relayed by Wednesday's mail. If the ruling is B or silence, KS-861 is the record.

## Detail

Round 2 closed what it was commissioned to close, and introduced one new hole:

- **F-7 CLOSED** on all six separator shapes — 403 / 0 upstream hits, both exact paths, enforcing; five red-proofs ran, the file is falsifiable. **F-8 CLOSED by removal** (grep 0 at head / 1 at parent, two positive controls, census re-derived at 32). F-1 and F-4 still closed; SETS 255 -> 260, shared 709/709, 0 failed.
- **F-9 - MAJOR, a regression this commit created.** `ERASURE_SUBPATH = /^\/erasures(\/|$)/` has no `i` flag while express matches case-insensitively (neither service sets `case sensitive routing`). Six spellings - `ERASURES`, `Erasures`, `//ERASURES`, `/API/GDPR/ERASURES`, `Erasures/`, `GET .../ERASURES/abc` - reach originate's erasure handler in **enforcing** mode for a `connector`-role key **without** the scope: precisely the population the cutover exists to refuse. The **parent refused five of them, 403 / 0 hits**. Grace mode also got worse - those spellings are now admitted with **zero** `[KS-843]` warns where the parent logged them.
- **F-10 - MAJOR, undisclosed coverage regression.** The test rewrite is **-3 / +2**, not -1. The removed `S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES` mint-set cell - the one that closed #841's F-2 - has **no successor anywhere in the repo** (`git grep -a 'S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES' 59248bf38 -- '*__tests__*'` = 0; parent = 2; positive control `platform.ts` = 2, so the product is fine and the test is gone). The commit message reports `255 -> 260` and does not mention the deletion.
- **F-11 - minor.** Every *admitted* erasure authenticates twice (gate chain + catch-all), doubling a remote `POST /api/keys/validate` on a partner-facing path. Refused requests authenticate once.

## Why the enforcement is a switch and not a gate
Kam ruled *"refuse others 403"*. It cannot be turned on in one step, and the reason is a measured absence rather than a preference:

**Platform K has no way to add a scope to an existing API key.** The security service's key surface is exactly `POST /api/keys` (create), `GET /api/keys` (list), `DELETE /api/keys/:id` (revoke), `POST /api/keys/validate` — no PATCH, no PUT, and no `UPDATE svc_api_keys` anywhere in the service. (Control: 9 `svc_api_keys` statements in that file, so the null is a real absence. My first sweep returned zero for the *wrong* reason — those routes are on `app.`, not `router.` — and a control caught it before it became a conclusion.)

So every connector key issued before this scope existed lacks it, and the only route to a scoped key is rotation, which is platform-admin-only by guardrail. A bare `requireScope` would 403 Platform S's live erasure path with no forward fix. Hence: role-or-scope, one structured log line per role-only admission, and `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED` to flip once the log shows S on a rotated key.

The flag is tested `=== 'true'`, so `"TRUE"`, `"1"`, `"yes"` or a typo leave the **grace on**. A misspelling must never silently start refusing a partner. That has its own cell.

## The lesson, recorded because it is field evidence
The mount-order cell — the one asserting both erasure routes are registered *before* the catch-all `/api/gdpr` mount — **went red on its first run.** It used a bare `indexOf` and matched the **comment** I had just written above those routes, which quotes the catch-all mount while explaining the ordering.

That is [KS-386](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-386) F-3's exact failure mode — prose read as code — **in a cell I wrote a few hours after shipping the fix for it.** It now matches a statement anchored to the start of a line, and carries a control proving it is not reading the prose.

**A rule does not transfer on its own.** Knowing F-3 did not stop me writing F-3 again; the cell caught me, not my memory of the lesson. That is the argument for cells over care.
